SMTO-BOOT-0042 — SMTO's optional Console couldn't start

GUID: 5c6009b8-4fa5-4267-bc5e-ebc09bfd7944
Slug: boot-console-start-failed
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • SMTO tried to start its Console, a separate diagnostics page, and the computer wouldn't start it. Your conversations and Tasks don't depend on the Console.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open SMTO in your browser as usual. If your conversations appear, you can keep working. The Console is an extra diagnostics page, and the rest of SMTO doesn't need it.
  2. If you need the Console, close programs you aren't using, then stop and start SMTO the way you normally do. A computer can refuse to start another program when it is short of memory or already running too many.
  3. If it still won't start, run ./install.sh again in the SMTO project folder, or reinstall the SMTO app, then start SMTO. The Console is started with SMTO's own Python, and a damaged installation can stop it from launching.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts without this message, and the Console page opens if you need it.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full message from SMTO's startup output and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change Model, permission or certificate settings to get around this; they aren't related.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Server could not create its optional diagnostic Console sidecar because subprocess.Popen raised OSError; the Server continued without the Console.

What this means

  • Optional Console sidecar creation raises OSError from subprocess.Popen and returns no child process. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • Optional Console sidecar creation raises OSError from subprocess.Popen and returns no child process.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the OS launch diagnostic and installed executable; this branch does not itself test whether a started server could bind its port.

How to fix it

  • Read the OSError in the Server's terminal output (missing or non-executable Python interpreter, permission denied, or process and memory limits such as EAGAIN or ENOMEM) and fix it. The web bundle launches the Console as smto_runtime.serve agent_runtime.console.app:create_console_app on AOR_CONSOLE_BIND_HOST:AOR_CONSOLE_PORT (default 8015); set AOR_CONSOLE_AUTOSTART=0 to stop launching it, or start it on demand with aor console.
  • Resolve the recorded process-launch or installation error for the optional Console and use its supported startup flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported sidecar can be launched while the controller's existing state remains preserved.

What not to do

  • Do not change unrelated model, execution or trust settings to bypass this failure.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
